title: Bridge Deck & Rhythm Reset

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-12 10:00 AM PDT — Duration: 74 minutes
Attendees: Jonah Reed, Maya Chen, Dr. Priya Nair, Liam Ortiz, Marcus Liu, Sofia Park, Evan Brooks

Auto-generated summary (may be partial): leadership reset for Q4 priorities, hiring cadence adjustment, incident follow-up, ops cost check

Topics: Q4 priorities; hiring freeze/exceptions; Dedicated capacity burst; incident postmortem; all-hands cadence

[00:00] Jonah: okay, let's go ahead and get started. thanks everyone for carving time this morning. we'll run about an hour, maybe a bit longer. objective is a short bridge deck and a rhythm reset for Q4. Maya's driving the deck.
[01:12] Maya: yep, hi everyone. quick slide 1 — purpose: tighten focus, reduce work-in-progress, and align on hiring. I'm gonna run through the top five asks. forgive me, uh, slides are up in the shared drive link — "Q4-bridge-deck-v2".
[03:05] Liam: real quick note, from eng perspective we have two infra hires that are blocking rollout of Dedicated pooling changes. without them we won't meet the latency SLOs for certain customers.
[04:10] Priya: and with the incident last week — the KV cache blowup — we saw tail latency regressions under mixed traffic and the mitigation took longer because of a couple of manual steps. I have a postmortem draft.
[05:30] Jonah: let's not gloss over that, please. Priya, can you summarize the critical remediation?
[06:12] Priya: sure. root cause is a stale cache invalidation path when the autoscaler spun down a node. shorthand: we lost coherent KV prefix state across shards. the fix is two-fold: short term — better throttling and automated invalidation; medium term — move to a bounded prefix cache with stronger lease semantics. I'm recommending two hires: a senior infra engineer to own caching & scheduler and a reliability SWE to own autoscaler hardening.
[08:00] Maya: note, those two roles are on the exception list. the proposal is a temporary pause on IC hiring for product and growth until we re-evaluate in 8 weeks, but we make exceptions for critical infra and sales/customer success roles that protect revenue.
[09:15] Evan: from sales side, customers asked about dedicated capacity SLA after the incident. they're sensitive to any availability hit; if we delay infra hires we risk churn on a couple of mid-market accounts.
[10:30] Marcus: ops side — we ran a cost blip when we added burst nodes last month. if we buy additional Dedicated pool capacity up front it's higher capex. I propose a small burst test this week with telemetry to validate unit economics before committing.
[12:00] Jonah: pragmatic. I want a 48-hour window on the deck changes and then sign-off. can we agree to review the revised deck by Monday?
[12:45] Maya: yes. I'll send the updated top-5 priorities doc by Thursday EOD.
[14:10] Sofia: on people side, we'll put out an organization note about the temporary hiring cadence change, an FAQ, and an exceptions process. we should be explicit about timelines and commitment to re-evaluate.
[15:22] Liam: one nuance — the build vs buy decision for the autoscaler bits. we have an internal prototype, but there's also a third-party partner (OpenCloud-ish) who has a managed autoscaler product. cost and lock-in are concerns.
[16:40] Priya: yeah, we evaluated that briefly; it wasn't fit for our KV semantics. also some of the vendors don't support the kind of KV cache coherence we need, so it would be a compromise.
[18:05] Jonah: competitors were named in the exec notes — Anthropic and Lambda Labs came up in a benchmarking thread — let's keep that in the notes but not a focus here.
[19:30] Maya: moving to roadmap tradeoffs — recommended: cut two non-core features, push them to Q1, and prioritize the caching/autoscaler work + observability improvements. that should reduce WIP and help hit our SLOs.
[21:00] Liam: OKR alignment: that means shifting two eng squads for ~6 weeks into a reliability pod. we'll need people leads to accept temporary reassignments.
[22:20] Jonah: do we have headcount runway for that, or do we need contractors?
[23:05] Marcus: runway is tight but doable if we halt non-essential capacity purchases. we'll reforecast. I'll pull a cost model and show the trade-off.
[24:40] Priya: also a reminder: the incident produced a gap in our runbook. I'm adding a new playbook for cache invalidation and cross-shard recovery. will share the draft.
[26:15] Maya: communications: we should do a technical town hall next Tuesday for engineers and customers can get a short update via sales for the affected accounts.
[27:30] Evan: sales would prefer a recorded technical note and a small FAQ for account teams — one-pager is best.
[28:50] Jonah: timeline check — can we commit to the two hires being expedited within two weeks pending exception approval?
[29:35] Liam: yes — we'll start interviews immediately but need exec sign-off for reqs.
[30:10] Maya: on cadence, proposal: move large all-hands from weekly to twice-monthly big syncs and insert 30-minute tactical pods weekly per org. idea is fewer long meetings and more focused async followups.
[31:55] Sofia: people impact: employees like predictability; we'll run a survey before changing cadence but I think this will increase deep-work windows.
[33:20] Jonah: let's pilot the cadence change in November.
[34:40] Marcus: ops follow-up — I'm going to run a 72-hour bench of Dedicated pool variations (different instance classes and quantization settings) to see cost vs latency. will need sample workload and a small budget for the test.
[36:05] Priya: for the benchmark, include mixed sequence lengths notably 512 and 2048 tokens; that surfaced the regression. also include some quantized model variants in the profile.
[37:30] Maya: product ask — cut one small feature in favor of observability sprint and push backlog items to next quarter.
[38:50] Liam: one more item — we should be careful with rollouts. the smart routing fallback worked but we should validate the fallback policy matrix in staging more often.
[40:05] Jonah: agreed. can we set a recurring test for fallback scenarios?
[40:55] Marcus: yes, ops will schedule a weekly chaos test for routing fallbacks.
[42:10] Evan: on renewal risk — two mid-market customers touched the incident; renewals coming up in January. sales needs firm SLAs and a remediation timeline to reduce churn risk.
[43:25] Maya: I will update the renewal playbook and share script for sales to use in account conversations.
[44:40] Sofia: hiring pause message draft will go out today and we will host an AMA next week to address questions.
[45:50] Priya: question from chat — is the KV cache change backward compatible with older model formats? short answer: yes but there's a migration window. we'll detail the plan.
[47:10] Jonah: ok, final recap — exceptions for infra and revenue-protecting roles; hiring pause for most ICs; two-week expedited hiring for infra; ops to run Dedicated burst test; Priya to circulate postmortem draft; cadence pilot in November; updated deck in 48 hours.
[48:30] Maya: I'll send the deck link and the top-5 priorities doc right after this call.
[49:15] Liam: I'll share the capacity reforecast and the reqs for the two hires.
[50:05] Marcus: I'll kick off the 72-hour bench and share telemetry dashboards.
[51:20] Sofia: People will send FAQ and host the AMA.
[52:40] Evan: Sales will prepare the customer-facing note and renewal talking points.
[54:00] Jonah: any other business?
[55:12] (brief silence)
[56:00] Jonah: thanks everyone. strong alignment. we'll reconvene if anything materializes — otherwise expect the updated deck in your inboxes within two days.
[57:25] (meeting adjourned)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., references to "KV cache" transcribed as "CV cache" in places; some speaker labels may be generic. Recorded audio quality: reasonably clean but a couple of speakers on mobile created minor dropouts.
